claims.text: The material family is face-centered-cubic high-entropy alloys derived from Fe-Co-Ni.
The targeted property for improvement is saturation magnetization.
The primary scientific challenge is accurate quantification and control of the orbital contribution to the total magnetic moment.
Orbital moments are often quenched in these alloys by strong crystal-field effects and complex chemical disorder.
Orbital-moment quenching makes prediction and enhancement of magnetic properties by first-principles calculations difficult.
Relevant Fe-Co-Ni-based fcc HEAs may contain Cr or Mn additions.
Relevant Fe-Co-Ni-based fcc HEAs may contain Al additions.
Tailoring local chemical order and composition through annealing or alloying could preserve the fcc phase while enhancing orbital contributions.
The proposed conditions span 50–1200 K and varying lattice parameters intended to represent thermal expansion.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations and magneto-volume coupling influence the magnetic behavior, magnetic entropy, and internal energy.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations induce thermal magnetic moments on Cr and Ni that are non-magnetic in static calculations.
The interplay of longitudinal spin fluctuations and crystal-field effects quenches the orbital moment and limits the total magnetic moment.
Precise control of local chemical environments and electronic structure can mitigate orbital-moment quenching.
The proposed intervention will improve saturation magnetization by increasing the orbital contribution to the total magnetic moment.
Magnetic transition temperatures in Fe-Co-Ni-derived HEAs are tunable by composition.
Some fcc Fe-Co-Ni-derived HEAs exhibit room-temperature paramagnetism.
Current fcc Fe-Co-Ni-based HEAs have lower saturation magnetization than conventional ferromagnetic alloys because their orbital moments are quenched.
The magnitude of the orbital contribution and its sensitivity to local chemical disorder are uncertain because of limitations in current first-principles methods.
